outcome: Glycemic control (fasting blood glucose, postprandial blood glucose)
cohort: The study included 89 pregnant women with pregestational diabetes mellitus receiving prenatal care in a public hospital in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, between 2009 and 2014.
finding: The carbohydrate counting method (CCM) showed a better effect on postprandial glycemia and was the only method that reduced fasting blood glucose throughout the intervention, although both methods contributed to reducing postprandial glycemia, with no differences observed for other maternal and perinatal outcomes.
mod_finding: Cesarean delivery was performed in 82% of the pregnant women and was associated with hypertensive disorders (gestational hypertension or pre-eclampsia).
